tagline: We walk your product like your customers do and map where they stumble
intro: Waypoint tests the everyday journeys in apps and websites: arriving, signing up, booking, paying. Our testers work through each route on real phones and laptops and hand you a map of every place someone got stuck.
audience: Booking, travel and marketplace products across Australia and New Zealand, from founders before a first launch to product teams shipping every fortnight.
pricing_note: A fixed price per journey map, quoted after a short call. Ongoing release testing runs on a monthly retainer you can pause between launches.

services.title: Journey maps
services.description: We walk every key route through your product once, end to end, and give you a map marking each place a customer gets confused, stuck or lost.

services.title: Pre-launch walkthroughs
services.description: In the fortnight before you launch, we test the new flows daily on the devices your customers own and file issues straight into your tracker.

services.title: Release check-ins
services.description: Before each release we re-walk the journeys that matter most, so a change in one corner does not quietly break booking or payment in another.

services.title: Real-world conditions
services.description: Slow trains, weak signal, a phone on low battery mode, a session that expires halfway through checkout. We test the journey where it actually happens.

process.title: Sketch the route
process.description: A short call to learn what your product does, who uses it and which journeys matter most. We send back a route and a fixed quote.

process.title: Walk every checkpoint
process.description: Our testers work through each journey on real devices and networks, writing up every stumble with steps, screenshots and the device used.

process.title: Hand over the map
process.description: You get the journey map, a prioritised list of issues and a walkthrough call. After fixes, we re-walk the route and tick it off.

proof.text: The journey map showed us three places people quit booking that we had never noticed.
